title: Samsung Launches Galaxy Card to Take On Apple in US Credit Card Market
excerpt: The Galaxy Card, issued by Barclays on the Visa network, offers 5% cash back on Samsung purchases and signals the Korean tech giant's broader ambitions in financial services.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Samsung launched the Galaxy Card on July 20, its first US credit card with Barclays.
  • The card offers 5% cash back on Samsung purchases and rewards on Samsung Pay transactions.
  • Users can manage accounts and redeem rewards entirely through Samsung Wallet.
  • Samsung plans to expand into savings accounts and other financial products beyond credit cards.
  • 70% of US households own at least one Samsung device, driving potential card adoption.
Samsung's Financial Ecosystem Expansion

›5% cash back on Samsung purchases.
›Integrated with Samsung Wallet for easy management.
›Plans for digital prepaid accounts and high-yield savings.

  • Samsung launched the Galaxy Card on July 20, its first US credit card, in partnership with Barclays and running on the Visa network.
  • The card offers 5% cash back on Samsung purchases and additional rewards on Samsung Pay transactions and other spending categories.
  • Users can apply, manage accounts, track spending and redeem rewards entirely through Samsung Wallet.
  • Samsung signalled plans to expand beyond cards into savings accounts and other financial products, positioning Samsung Wallet as a comprehensive financial hub.

Samsung Enters Financial Services

Samsung Electronics officially entered the US credit card market on Monday with the launch of the Galaxy Card, a co-branded product with Barclays that puts the Korean tech giant in direct competition with Apple's established Card offering.

https://x.com/Samsung/status/2079341102243676284

The Galaxy Card, which runs on Visa's network, is available as both a virtual card inside Samsung Wallet and a premium physical card featuring a black Samsung logo. It offers 5% cash back on Samsung purchases — including device preorders — with additional reward tiers for Samsung Pay transactions and general spending, according to Reuters.

The Scale Argument

Samsung is betting on its massive US hardware footprint to drive adoption. Seventy percent of US households own at least one Samsung device, and nearly 30% own three or more, according to Sih Lee, executive vice president and head of North America Fintech Business at Samsung Electronics.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=TBHuntc4jb8

The card is fully integrated into Samsung Wallet, allowing users to apply, manage accounts, track spending and redeem rewards without leaving the app. Doug Villone, head of cards and partnerships at Barclays US Consumer Bank, described the digital-first design as aimed at customers who increasingly manage finances through mobile devices rather than physical wallets.

"The relationship that we're building with Barclays is a strategic and long-term relationship. We do have intention to collaborate and explore all avenues of different products and different capabilities."

— Sih Lee, EVP, Samsung Electronics North America Fintech

Beyond Cards

Samsung made clear the Galaxy Card is a starting point, not the destination. Lee signalled the company's ambition to expand into digital prepaid accounts, high-yield savings options and potentially buy-now-pay-later services — mirroring Apple's own evolution from a simple card to a broader financial ecosystem within Apple Wallet.

The timing is strategic. The launch comes ahead of Samsung's Unpacked event and positions the Galaxy Card alongside the company's hardware refresh cycle, creating a natural cross-selling opportunity with new device purchases.

The Apple Card Comparison

Apple launched its Card in 2019 and it remains available only in the US. Apple initially partnered with Goldman Sachs for the Mastercard-branded product, though the relationship proved challenging for the bank. Samsung's partnership with Barclays — a traditional consumer bank with established credit infrastructure — may offer a more stable foundation.

The 5% Samsung cash back on device purchases matches Apple's highest reward tier, while the broader integration with Samsung Pay targets the daily transaction volume that makes a credit card sticky. Samsung Wallet has struggled to gain the traction of Apple Pay in the US market, and a branded credit card could change that dynamic by giving users a financial reason to keep Samsung's payment ecosystem front and centre.

What It Means for Consumers

For the roughly 140 million Samsung device owners in the US, the Galaxy Card offers a loyalty play: earn rewards for staying in the Samsung ecosystem, spend them on Samsung products. For the broader fintech market, it represents another step in the convergence of hardware, software and financial services that has characterised the smartphone era's second act.
